Definition: properly, something very smooth; i.e. a treacherous spot; figuratively, blandishment
BiblicalUsage: Chalaqlaqqah means slippery places, and by extension flattery. The psalmist prays his enemies' way will be dark and slippery, Jeremiah says the prophets' way will be slippery in the darkness, and Daniel says the vile king will obtain the kingdom by flatteries, and many will cleave to him with flatteries.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe slippery ground and smooth words are the same danger: the prophets slip in the dark, and the king slips into the kingdom on flattery. God makes the way slippery for those who make it smooth for themselves.
